gp.text: The following tables present revenues and gross profit (loss) for the Company and its reportable segments by product line for the three months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025.

ga.heading: Selling, General and Administrative Expenses
ga.text: Consolidated SG&A for the six months ended June 30 was 7.5% of revenues in 2026 compared with 8.3% in the prior-year period as revenue growth outpaced the increase in these expenses.

sga.heading: Selling, General and Administrative Expenses (SG&A)
sga.text: Consolidated SG&A for the second quarter of 2026 was 5.9% of revenues compared with 6.5% in the prior-year quarter as revenue growth outpaced the increase in these expenses.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text: For the six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, the effective income tax rates for continuing operations were 23.3% and 20.3%, respectively. The higher 2026 effective income tax rate compared with 2025 was primarily attributable to the revaluation of deferred tax liabilities driven by changes in the state jurisdictional mix of the business following the QUIKRETE transaction.

ocf.heading: Cash Provided by Operating Activities
ocf.text:
Cash provided by operating activities for the six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025 was $339 million and $605 million, respectively. Operating cash flow is substantially derived from consolidated net earnings before deducting depreciation, depletion and amortization and the impact of changes in working capital requirements. In the six months ended June 30, 2026, operating cash flow reflects the deduction of the noncash gain on the QUIKRETE transaction from net earnings and the higher income tax payments related to the gain on the QUIKRETE transaction.

The seasonal nature of construction activity impacts the Company’s interim operating cash flow when compared with the full year. Full-year 2025 net cash provided by operating activities was $1.8 billion.

da.text: The following table displays depreciation, depletion and amortization by product line included in the Costs of revenues line item in the consolidated statements of earnings and comprehensive earnings.

capex.text: Cash on hand, along with the Company’s projected internal cash flows and availability of financing resources, including its access to debt and equity capital markets, is expected to remain sufficient to provide the capital resources necessary to support anticipated operating needs, cover debt service requirements, meet capital expenditures and discretionary investment needs, fund certain acquisition opportunities that may arise, allow for payment of dividends for the foreseeable future and allow the repurchase of shares of the Company’s common stock. At June 30, 2026, the Company had $742 million of unused borrowing capacity under its Revolving Facility and Trade Receivable Facility, subject to complying with the related leverage covenant. Historically, the Company has successfully extended the maturity dates of these credit facilities.

intro.text: Martin Marietta, a member of the S&P 500 Index, is an American-based company and a leading supplier of aggregates and other building materials. Through a network of operations spanning 29 states, Canada and The Bahamas, dedicated Martin Marietta teams supply the resources necessary for building the solid foundations on which our communities thrive. Martin Marietta’s Specialties business provides high-purity magnesia and dolomitic lime products used worldwide in environmental, industrial, agricultural and specialty applications. For more information, visit www.martinmarietta.com or www.magnesiaspecialties.com .

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
